title: Types of computer by method of operation
competency: Distinguish analog, digital and hybrid computers.

keywords.def: A computer that works with continuous data such as speed or temperature, e.g. a speedometer.
A computer that works with discrete data in the form of digits.
A computer with features of both analog and digital computers, e.g. in a petrol pump.

en.text: By method of operation there are three types. Analog computers work with continuous data such as speed, temperature or pressure and show a reading on a dial, like a speedometer or a mercury thermometer. Digital computers work with discrete data in the form of digits, using stored programs. Hybrid computers combine both: they convert analog signals to digital, as in a petrol pump that turns fuel flow into quantity and price.

screens.title: The needle
screens.ask: A car's needle speedometer moves smoothly as the car speeds up. What kind of data is this?
screens.after: Continuous: it changes smoothly, not in steps. Analog computers use continuous data.

screens.title: Three types by operation
paras: Analog: continuous data; accepts data directly from measuring devices; output on a dial or scale; limited memory.
Digital: discrete values (digits); stored programs; fast calculations and logical operations.
Hybrid: both continuous and discrete; converts analog signals to digital before processing; used in petrol pumps, airplanes, hospitals.
